label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Here's a draft. Fill in the bracketed spots with your name and details before you sign.

---

[Your full name]
Bus Operator, Bus 41
[District / Transportation Department name]
Dayton, Ohio

November __, 2026

Mrs. Okafor
c/o [Transportation Office name and address]

**Re: Statement regarding the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Bus 41, Route 9, Kessler Ave and Brandt St**

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing in response to the complaint you filed with the Transportation Office on October 29. My supervisor, Darlene, gave me a copy on November 3 and asked me to put my account in writing. I want to give you a clear picture of what happened that afternoon, and I want you to know I take your concerns seriously. I drive Amara every day, and I care how she and you feel about riding my bus.

**What happened**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was driving the afternoon run on Bus 41, Route 9, for Fairmont Elementary. Amara is a kindergartner, and her bag carries the green tag that means an adult must be at the stop to receive her. Her stop is at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street.

I reached the stop at 3:52, two minutes after the scheduled time of 3:50. I opened the door and waited. I looked up and down the corner and did not see an adult there for Amara. I waited until about 3:55.

District policy for kindergarten riders is clear. If no adult is at the stop, the student stays on the bus and is returned to school, and the school office contacts the parent. I followed that rule. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch, and Gloria at dispatch called the school to let them know Amara was coming back. I still had three more stops to make and 14 children on the bus, so I could not leave the bus or delay the other children any longer.

I brought Amara back to Fairmont at 4:31. I walked her inside myself and handed her directly to Mrs. Petrakis in the main office.

**How Amara was**

I want you to know Amara was fine the whole time. She sat and colored on her folder. At one point she asked me if she could ride some more. I told her we were taking a little extra trip, and she seemed happy with that. She was not crying and she did not appear upset. I understand that does not take away how frightening it must have been for you when you could not find her, and I do not mean it that way. I only want you to know how she was while she was in my care.

**What you saw from across the street**

I understand you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved to me. I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, and it blocked my view. I am not saying this to place blame on anyone. I am telling you what I could and could not see from the driver's seat.

I also understand you were told I "drove off laughing." I was not laughing. As I pulled away from the stop, I was telling a fourth grader in seat 2 to sit back down. If it looked to you like I was laughing, or like I was ignoring you, I am sorry for that. I would never wave off a parent on purpose.

I also could not get off the bus and look across the road. With 14 children aboard, I cannot leave them unattended, and I am not permitted to. That is why I rely on seeing the adult at the stop from where I sit.

**A request for the camera footage**

The camera on Bus 41 recorded the stop. I am asking the Transportation Office to pull and review that footage for October 27. I believe it will show the time I arrived, how long I waited, what was and was not visible at the corner, and the box truck on Brandt Street. I want the record to be accurate, and I would like both you and the office to be able to see it for yourselves.

**My view of the decision**

I will be honest with you. I am not going to apologize for following the policy, because I believe it is there to protect children like Amara. Her safety was the reason I did what I did. Letting a five-year-old off a bus at an empty corner is not something I am willing to do, and I do not believe you would want me to. I have done this job for 28 years without a single write-up, and I have always tried to do it carefully.

I have grandchildren of my own, and I know how it feels to worry about a little one. I am sorry that Amara's afternoon, and yours, turned out to be so upsetting. I wish it had gone differently for you.

**Going forward**

I have one request that I think would help prevent this from happening again. When Amara is being picked up at the stop, would you please stand on the same side of the street as the bus, or step out of your car where I can see you? If I can see you, I will release her to you right away. Even if I cannot see you, I will be looking for you at that stop, and I want to hand her off to you without any trouble.

I would be glad to keep driving Amara. She is a sweet girl, and I look forward to seeing her each afternoon. I want this resolved so that she can ride with me comfortably, and so that you feel confident about it too. If you would like to speak with me, or if you would like to talk it through with Darlene or the Transportation Office present, I am willing to do that.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.

Respectfully,

[Signature]
[Your printed name]
Bus Operator, Bus 41
[Employee ID, if the office uses one]

cc: Darlene [last name], Transportation Supervisor
Employee file

---

A couple of notes:

- I left out the story about the family from years back who thanked you. In a letter to Mrs. Okafor it can read like you're comparing her to someone else. If you want it in anyway, I can add a line.
- Check the times against your own notes before you sign. If your 3:55 wait was closer to 3:54 or 3:56, use the real number.
- If you know Mrs. Petrakis's first name or Gloria's last name, you can add them, but it's fine as is.
